summary: Connect native world bounds, candidate pairs, contact-plan publication and analytic manifolds in a resident device program.
regressions: 26 reset/publication cases cover capacity clamping, maximum u32 totals, exact ceiling division, batches, indirect grids and guards.
17 connected ball/box scenes cover empty, single, tail/grid-stride, batched, rotated, separated and filtered collisions.
Pair permutation is accepted only with the associated manifold; corrupted ownership, materials, IDs, counters, guards and unsupported geometry are rejected.
Exact-source validation includes native inert-link and stable edge-intersection fixes 0031 and 0032.
Repeated native fixture export preserves a fixed explicit input ABI and existing runtime artifacts.

Box geometry validation checks both native and ported endpoints against their box surfaces; small scale-bounded coordinate/depth roundoff is accepted while off-surface, large-error and material/normal mutations fail.
differences: The pinned TileLang Metal/Ascend backends reject atomic_load; atomic add-zero provides the required read without changing counter values. No hardware synchronization claim for Ascend.
A fixed nonzero narrow-phase launch uses the native grid-stride loop and device ContactPlan. Native indirect grids are still produced and checked.
Atomic pair order is unspecified. Validation reorders expected manifolds by pair identity; runtime executes no host geometry or sorting.

This connected pipeline currently accepts only balls/cuboids and capacity sufficient for every pair. Generic PFM, meshes/polylines, truncated scene candidates and full scene solving remain unimplemented.
Broad phase, analytic narrow phase and the collision program now share a single Rust-derived collision layout exporter.

Composed box-box point coordinates and separation distances use max(2e-6, 32*f32_epsilon*local_scale) absolute tolerance plus the existing relative tolerance. The 2.45e-6 residual after the native line-intersection repair is ordinary scalar/SIMD transform roundoff; both endpoints must independently lie on the box surfaces. Material and normal tolerances are unchanged.
